part.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `renderComponent` in src/diff/index.js: the `_stateCallbacks` → `_renderCallbacks` migration loop ran before the pre-render lifecycles and re-assigned `c._stateCallbacks = []` inside the loop, so after a `setState(update, callback)` queued during `componentDidMount` (e.g. from an observable subscription), only the first callback survived and later ones were orphaned/never executed.

The fix mirrors upstream preact 10.11.2 (the actual fix for this issue):
- Removed the early migration loop before the lifecycle methods.
- Drain all `_stateCallbacks` into `_renderCallbacks` in the skipped-update branch (`shouldComponentUpdate === false`), so callbacks still fire even when a render is skipped.
- Drain them right after `render()` in the class-component branch, so callbacks queued during the current render pass (including via deferred renders after subscriptions) are flushed on commit.

Validation:
- The previously failing FAIL_TO_PASS test `#componentDidMount › supports multiple setState callbacks` now passes.
